26 A source of sound waves with constant frequency moves towards a stationary observer.
The observer compares the sound waves arriving at the observer’s position with the waves
emitted by the source of sound.
What is detected by the observer?
A
a decreased frequency of the sound waves
B
no change in frequency of the sound waves
C
a decreased wavelength of the sound waves
D
no change in wavelength of the sound waves

hints: Notice the source has constant frequency but moves towards the stationary observer, so think about where each successive wavefront is emitted in air.
Recall that sound speed $v$ in still air is fixed, so the distance the source advances between emissions reduces the spacing of wavefronts ahead of it.
Use $v = f\lambda$ for the waves arriving at the observer to connect that changed spacing to the observed frequency.
walkthrough: Identify the setup: source frequency $f_s$ is constant, wave speed $v$ in air is constant, source speed $v_s$ is towards the stationary observer.
State the physical cause: in one period $T = 1/f_s$ the source moves distance $v_s T$ forward, so the next wavefront is emitted from a position closer to the observer.
Set up the observed wavelength: emitted wavelength is $\lambda_s = v/f_s$, but ahead of the source the spacing becomes $\lambda_{obs} = vT - v_s T = (v - v_s)/f_s$.
Compare: since $v - v_s < v$, then $\lambda_{obs} < \lambda_s$, so the observer detects a decreased wavelength.
Link to frequency: with $v = f_{obs} \lambda_{obs}$ and $v$ unchanged, a smaller $\lambda_{obs}$ means a larger $f_{obs}$, ruling out decreased or unchanged frequency.

A.explanation: Frequency increases, not decreases, when a constant-frequency source moves towards a stationary observer.

B.explanation: The observed frequency changes because successive wavefronts arrive more often due to motion of the source.

C.explanation: Motion towards the observer crowds successive wavefronts together, so observed $\lambda$ is shorter than emitted $\lambda$.

D.explanation: Wavelength at the observer is not unchanged because the source moves a distance towards the observer between emissions.
